trip_plan.totalNote: Three days: backpack to Fish Creek Pass, climb the Northwest Ridge as a long technical day from camp, and hike out.

days.title: Hike in to Fish Creek Pass
days.objective: Camp near Fish Creek Pass or at Star Lake
days.note: Backpack in on the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail to a camp at Star Lake or near Fish Creek Pass.

days.title: Climb the Northwest Ridge
days.objective: Summit Star Peak via the ridge
days.note: Climb the ridge as a technical day trip from camp, allowing a full day for the approach and the ridge's sustained, low-angle length before the crux. The descent off the ridge is undocumented, so settle on a strategy (downclimb or rappel the ridge, or drop west to the Southwest Spur scramble) before committing above the…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the West Fork Buttermilk Trailhead
days.note: Hike back out the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail to the trailhead.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, ~18.6-mile backpack trip (one night in, one summit day, one night out) that lines up with the 4,730 ft gain / 18.6 mi round trip; very fit parties have pushed it car-to-car in a single ~18-20 hour day, but that's an outlier, not the recommended plan.

days.title: Backpack in to Star Lake basecamp
days.objective: Reach Star Lake camp (~7,200 ft)
days.note: Hike the West Fork Buttermilk Creek Trail up to Star Lake, the standard basecamp for Star Peak. The trail is steep and increasingly brushy/poorly maintained in its upper miles, so this is a slower 7.5-mile carry than the mileage alone suggests. Camp at least 200 ft from the lakeshore per wilderness rules.

days.title: Summit day: Star Peak
days.objective: Climb Star Peak (8,693 ft) from Star Lake camp
days.note: Drop the overnight pack and go light: up the scree bowl south of the lake to the pass, contour around point 7912, then follow the SW ridge east to the summit. It's technically easy but slow, loose scree/talus travel with some easy hands-and-feet scrambling near the top. Strong parties often tag Courtney and/or Oval Pea…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the West Fork Buttermilk Creek trailhead
days.note: Break camp and reverse Day 1's route back down to the trailhead. Mostly downhill but the same brushy, sometimes hard-to-follow tread makes it slower going than a groomed trail of this length.

camps_on_file.name: Star Lake

trip_plan.totalNote: A standard 2-day/1-night backpack: ~19 miles round trip with roughly 5,600 ft of gain, camping one night at Cooney Lake and day-scrambling Switchback Mountain's Class 2-3 Southeast Ridge before hiking fully out.

days.title: Approach to Cooney Lake camp
days.objective: Reach Cooney Lake and set up base camp
days.note: From the Foggy Dew Creek Trailhead (~3,430 ft), follow Foggy Dew Creek Trail #417 up through forest and past Foggy Dew Falls, then at the trail's end take the Martin Creek Trail north to the Cooney Lake trail and the lake. Established campsites sit near the outlet (~7,200 ft) with views toward the Sawtooth Ridge peaks.

days.title: Summit push and hike out
days.objective: Scramble Switchback Mountain, then pack out to the trailhead
days.note: Leave camp with light packs before sunrise and climb about a mile above Cooney Lake to Cooney Pass and follow Switchback Mountain's broad Southeast Ridge, an easy Class 2-3 scramble to the 8,321 ft summit. After descending to camp, break it down and hike the full 7.8 miles back out to the trailhead the same day — a lon…

camps_on_file.name: Cooney Lake
Upper Eagle Lake and Horsehead Pass
camps_on_file.notes: The hub of the southern Sawtooth and the practical base for Switchback Mountain, with Hoodoo and Raven Ridge also within reach along the crest. Access is the Gold Creek side, not the Twisp River: turn off the highway onto the North Fork Gold Creek road, then a signed spur for several miles to the Eagle Lakes trailhead …

days.title: Day 1
days.note: Ferry/floatplane to Stehekin, hike Company Creek Trail (~3 mi) to the leave-trail point.

days.title: Day 2
days.note: Traverse White Goat Mountain's west slopes and cross the ~7,200 ft pass above Bird Lakes to a high bivy in the Bird Lakes basin.

days.title: Day 3
days.note: Climb the East Face (class 2-4 with a 5.4-5.6 crux) to the summit and return to camp.

days.title: Day 4
days.note: Hike out to Stehekin.

name: South Ridge (via Asa Peak NE Ridge)

trip_plan.totalNote: A 5-day trip from High Bridge: PCT to a Swamp Creek camp, off-trail to Upper Blue Basin and a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass, a very long summit day via the south ridge and chimney crux, and a long hike out.

days.title: High Bridge to Swamp Creek camp
days.objective: Reach a camp in the Swamp Creek area
days.note: Hike the PCT from High Bridge about 8.5 miles to a camp in the Swamp Creek area, roughly 5.2 hours.

days.title: Climb to Upper Blue Basin
days.objective: Reach camp in Upper Blue Basin
days.note: Cross Agnes Creek and Spruce Creek on logs, then climb steeply off-trail through brush, talus and slabs to a camp in Upper Blue Basin at about 5,000 ft.

days.title: Move to Icy-Spruce Pass high camp
days.objective: Reach a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass
days.note: Move camp up to a high camp near Icy-Spruce Pass at about 6,760 ft.

days.title: Summit via the south ridge
days.objective: Summit via the south ridge and chimney crux
days.note: Make the summit push via the south ridge and its chimney crux, about 8.5 hours up and 7 hours back to high camp for a typical party (a slower party took 10.6 up and 8.8 down). Return to high camp.

days.title: Hike out to High Bridge
days.objective: Return to High Bridge
days.note: Break camp and hike out to High Bridge.

trip_plan.totalNote: Ferry to Stehekin and hike the Stehekin River and Devore Creek trails to Bird Creek Camp, make an 8-9 hour round trip to Flora's 8,323-ft summit, and hike out to catch the return boat.

days.title: Stehekin to Bird Creek Camp
days.objective: Reach Bird Creek Camp (4,200 ft)
days.note: Take the ferry or floatplane from Chelan to Stehekin Landing and the NPS shuttle to Harlequin Bridge. Hike the Stehekin River Trail (about 3 miles) and the Devore Creek Trail (about 4 miles, steep then brushy) to Bird Creek Camp at 4,200 ft.

days.title: Summit Flora Mountain
days.objective: Round trip from camp to the 8,323-ft summit
days.note: Make a round-trip summit push from Bird Creek Camp via the saddle south of Enigma Peak, the Castle Creek crossing and the southwest ridge talus to the 8,323-ft summit and back, typically 8-9 hours.

days.title: Hike out and catch the ferry
days.objective: Return to Stehekin for the ferry
days.note: Hike out to Stehekin and catch the return shuttle and ferry.

camps_on_file.name: Bird Creek Camp
camps_on_file.notes: The only designated camp on the upper Devore Creek trail, just before the Bird Creek crossing. Parties base here and climb Flora in a long day, 4 to 5 hours up. Higher camps are possible in the larch basin around 6,500 to 6,900 ft.

camps_on_file.name: Purple Point and Harlequin — the landing camps, and the boat that decides the trip
camps_on_file.notes: Read this before any other site in the zone. Stehekin has no road to it. The only practical way in is the scheduled passenger boat up Lake Chelan from Chelan or Fields Point Landing, and the timetable, not your fitness, sets the shape of the trip. The slow boat takes roughly four hours each way and the express about tw…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, ~24-mile round-trip backpack via ferry/shuttle to High Bridge and the Agnes Creek/Swamp Creek Trail, built around one long summit day that gains roughly 5,100 ft on exposed Class 3-4 terrain above camp.

days.title: Approach to Swamp Creek camp
days.objective: Establish base camp at Swamp Creek
days.note: Ferry/shuttle to Stehekin then High Bridge, then a leisurely 9-mile hike on the PCT/Agnes Creek Trail up-valley to Swamp Creek, gaining about 1,200 ft along the way. Camp here and scout the route for tomorrow.

days.title: Needle Peak north ridge
days.objective: Summit Needle Peak (7,896 ft) and return to camp
days.note: The crux day: leave the unmaintained Swamp Creek Trail around 3,200 ft, work up through brush and slabs below the north face, and climb the west gully on the north ridge, weaving through cliff bands on a sustained, exposed Class 3-4 crux around 7,300-7,400 ft before a final loose gully to the summit block.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to High Bridge and catch the shuttle/ferry
days.note: Break camp and hike back down the Agnes Creek Trail/PCT to High Bridge, then pick up the shuttle to Stehekin and the ferry/floatplane back to Chelan.

camps_on_file.name: Swamp Creek Camp — the base for Needle Peak, Mount Lyall and Lyall Ridge
camps_on_file.notes: About nine miles south of High Bridge on the Pacific Crest Trail and roughly three beyond Fivemile, this is the working base for Needle Peak, Mount Lyall at 7,892 ft and the ridge between them. The unmaintained Swamp Creek trail leaves the corridor here and climbs toward Needle Peak's north ridge; the ground above is c…

camps_on_file.name: Purple Point and Harlequin — the landing camps, and the boat that decides the trip
camps_on_file.notes: Read this before any other site in the zone. Stehekin has no road to it. The only practical way in is the scheduled passenger boat up Lake Chelan from Chelan or Fields Point Landing, and the timetable, not your fitness, sets the shape of the trip. The slow boat takes roughly four hours each way and the express about tw…

camps_on_file.name: High Bridge Camp — the shuttle terminus and the base for McGregor Mountain
camps_on_file.notes: The bus stops here and the walking starts here, so almost every trip in this zone passes through it. Its own summit is McGregor Mountain, whose trail leaves the valley road near the guard station a mile or so from the bridge and is one of the biggest sustained climbs in the state: about 7.7 miles and 6,400 ft of gain t…

camps_on_file.name: Fivemile Camp, Agnes Creek
camps_on_file.notes: Five miles south of High Bridge on the Pacific Crest Trail through Agnes Gorge, this is the junction camp and the last comfortable night before things get serious. It is the departure point for Agnes Mountain — the West Fork Agnes Creek trail leaves here heading west, and it is the start of the standard approach to the…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day trip is standard: a long, brushy approach to a basin bivy, then a big second day that climbs the 8-pitch Southeast Ridge and pushes all the way back to the car (~13 hrs); a 3rd day is a common safety-margin option for the exit.

days.title: Long approach to basin bivy
days.objective: Reach a bivy site in the basin below Argonaut's east side
days.note: From the Beverly Turnpike trailhead, hike over Fourth Creek Pass, descend to Ingalls Creek and ford it, then climb steep, vegetated slopes toward the basin below Argonaut's southeast ridge. Expect real bushwhacking and slow going in the upper section.

days.title: Southeast Ridge to the summit, then all the way out
days.objective: Climb the Southeast Ridge and descend to the trailhead
days.note: Climb the 8-pitch Southeast Ridge to the summit, then descend the South Gully, return to camp, break camp, and hike the long approach out in the same push. This is a long day — many parties choose to camp a second night instead of finishing the exit.

camps_on_file.name: Ingalls Creek valley camps below the Sherpa and Argonaut south sides
camps_on_file.notes: This is the base for the south side of both Argonaut and Sherpa, and it is what makes those peaks feasible as overnights rather than brutal single pushes. Two ways in. From Esmeralda you climb to Longs Pass at about 6,200 feet and drop roughly 1,400 feet to the valley, then walk east along the trail until you are under…

camps_on_file.name: Beverly and De Roux campgrounds and the North Fork Teanaway roadside camps
camps_on_file.notes: This is what most parties on Ingalls Peak actually use, because all three Ingalls summits are comfortably a long day from the car and there is no reason to carry a camp. Sleeping on the road puts you at the Esmeralda trailhead in minutes rather than driving up from Cle Elum in the dark. The Ingalls group sits entirely …

trip_plan.totalNote: Standard plan is 2 days (basin bivy + a big summit/exit day, ~14.5 hrs); strong parties also do the whole thing car-to-car in a single ~17 hr push, and some parties stretch it to 3 relaxed days with side-scrambles of Colchuck or Dragontail.

days.title: Approach to basin camp
days.objective: Reach a camp in the basin below Argonaut's north side
days.note: Hike from the Stuart Lake trailhead via Mountaineer Creek, then bushwhack up toward the basin below the couloir/notch, camping near water in the north basin around 6,400 ft.

days.title: Couloir, NW Arete, and out
days.objective: Climb to the notch, up the arête, and exit to the trailhead
days.note: Climb the approach couloir to the notch, then 7 pitches up the Northwest Arête (mostly Class 4-5.6) to the summit. Descend east with about four rappels to the Argonaut-Colchuck col, drop back into the basin, break camp, and hike out.

camps_on_file.name: Argonaut north basin bivies, below the Colchuck-Argonaut col
camps_on_file.notes: From the bench in Mountaineer Creek the valley forks around 4,800 feet; take the easternmost fork and climb toward the col between Colchuck and Argonaut, and the flat ground in the basin at roughly this height is the high camp for the Northeast Couloir and the Northwest Arete. It puts the foot of the couloir within an …

campsite_pins.name: Lower basin below Argonaut's north face

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day trip: a moderate approach to an Ingalls Creek camp, then one long summit day of about 13.5 hours that climbs the 3-pitch South Face and hikes all the way back to the car.

days.title: Approach to Ingalls Creek camp
days.objective: Reach camp at the Ingalls Creek crossing
days.note: Hike in from the Beverly Creek trailhead over Fourth Creek trail and down to Ingalls Creek, fording to camp around 4,200 ft.

days.title: South Face to the summit, then out
days.objective: Climb the South Face and exit to the trailhead
days.note: Bushwhack and scramble up to the base of the South Face, climb 3 pitches to the summit, then reverse with rappels/downclimbing back to camp, break camp, and hike out the same day.

From Esmeralda you climb to Longs Pass at about 6,200 feet and drop roughly 1,400 feet to the valley, then walk east along the trail until you are under…

camps_on_file.notes: This is what most parties on Ingalls Peak actually use, because all three Ingalls summits are comfortably a long day from the car and there is no reason to carry a camp. Sleeping on the road puts you at the Esmeralda trailhead in minutes rather than driving up from Cle Elum in the dark. The Ingalls group sits entirely …

campsite_pins.name: Fourth Creek / Ingalls Creek confluence camp

trip_plan.totalNote: A standard 3-day, 2-night trip: ~9-10.5 mile carries on the in/out days (~6,000 ft each way) bracketing a long ~9-9.5 hour, ~2,300 ft round-trip summit day from a core Enchantment basecamp; very fit parties compress the summit push and hike-out into one very long single day.

days.title: Hike in to core Enchantment basin
days.objective: Establish camp near Perfection/Inspiration Lake
days.note: From the Snow Lakes trailhead (~1,300 ft), climb the long, steadily steepening Snow Lakes Trail past Nada and Snow Lakes and up into the core Enchantment basin, camping near Perfection or Inspiration Lake (~7,100-7,200 ft). A Core Enchantment Zone overnight permit is required in season and is hard to draw/walk up for.

days.title: Climb Cannon Mountain from camp
days.objective: Tag the Cannon Mountain summit and return to camp
days.note: A long out-and-back day-climb from camp: up past Talisman/Rune Lakes to Prusik Pass, northwest around Lorelei Lakelets and up onto Druid Plateau, then west up scree/snow to the summit block and a final friction-slab scramble. This typically takes roughly 9-9.5 hours round trip in good conditions; expect longer if snow …

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Break camp and return to the Snow Lakes trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach: descend from the core basin back down the Snow Lakes Trail past Snow and Nada Lakes to the trailhead. Knees take a beating on the steep switchbacks below Snow Lakes; many parties budget extra time versus the hike in.

camps_on_file.name: Snow Lakes
camps_on_file.notes: Common base for climbing Cannon from the Snow Lakes side, about 6.5 miles up the trail; the summit day continues past Lake Viviane into the upper basin.

camps_on_file.name: Nada Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The eastern staging camp, five and a half miles and about seventeen hundred feet of gain up the Snow Lakes trail from Icicle Creek Road, and the only road in the region that is open year round rather than gated through winter. It is the base for Cannon Mountain's southeast approach, which continues past Snow Lakes and …

trip_plan.totalNote: Standard trip is 2 days: backpack ~6.5 mi to a permitted 7,100 ft camp near Little Lake Caroline, then a long summit day (Class 3-4 scrambling) that finishes with a full hike-out to the car; the fittest parties instead do the whole ~17 mi, 5,300+ ft round trip car-to-car in one 10-14 hour day.

days.title: Backpack to high camp below the West Ridge
days.objective: Reach the ~7,100 ft camp near Little Lake Caroline
days.note: Hike the Eightmile Lake trail past Eightmile Lake to Lake Caroline, continue to Little Lake Caroline, then leave trail and angle cross-country (NE) through meadows and light timber to a flat camp area at ~7,100 ft below Cashmere's west side. This is the standard overnight base for the West Ridge.

days.title: Summit push and hike out
days.objective: Scramble the West Ridge to the summit, then pack out to the trailhead
days.note: Leave most gear at camp and climb light to the 8,000 ft col, then follow the west ridge and a short class 3-4 gully to the 8,514 ft summit — a few parties place a hand line on the exposed ledges near the top. Reverse the scramble back to camp, then break camp and hike all the way back out to the car the same day.

camps_on_file.name: Lake Caroline and Little Caroline
camps_on_file.notes: Cashmere Mountain does not belong to the Stuart Lake, Snow Lakes or Teanaway approaches at all; it is climbed from the Eightmile Lake trailhead on its own road off Icicle Creek. The West Ridge goes past Little Eightmile Lake, right at the junction onto the Eightmile to Trout Creek trail, over the ridge and down to Lake…

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip for most parties: hike in and camp, a long aid-climbing day, then hike out; very strong/fast aid teams could compress this to a single very long day.

days.title: Hike in to Colchuck Lake
days.objective: Establish camp at Colchuck Lake
days.note: The Tempest is a serious 9-pitch aid line, slower per pitch than the free routes on this wall, so most parties base out of a Colchuck Lake camp rather than pushing it car-to-car.

days.title: Climb The Tempest
days.objective: Aid/free climb all 9 pitches and return to camp
days.note: Alpine start from camp up to the base, then a long day of aid and free climbing on sustained 5.9-5.11/A2 terrain before rappelling back down to the basin.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the trailhead
days.note: An easy morning hike back down to the car after a long climbing day.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 2-day trip: hike in and camp at Colchuck Lake, then a long alpine-start summit day (~11 hrs) climbing the couloir and descending the Colchuck Glacier route.

days.title: Approach to Colchuck Lake camp
days.objective: Reach Colchuck Lake and set up camp for a pre-dawn couloir start
days.note: Hike from the Stuart Lake trailhead through forest and a boulder field to Colchuck Lake (~5,570 ft). Most parties camp lakeside rather than push straight through, since the couloir wants to be climbed before the sun softens it.

days.title: Northeast Couloir summit push
days.objective: Climb the Northeast Couloir and summit, then descend via the Colchuck Glacier route
days.note: Alpine start to cross the moraine/glacier by starlight and be in the couloir before rockfall/icefall starts once the sun hits it. The couloir is Grade II-III, roughly 6 pitches of steep snow/ice up to 60 degrees, then a short scramble to the summit. Descend the easier Colchuck Glacier route back to camp, break it down,…

camps_on_file.name: Colchuck Lake designated campsites
camps_on_file.notes: This is the working basecamp for Backbone Ridge, Serpentine Arete and Colchuck Balanced Rock, and it cuts an hour or more off the pre-dawn walk-in. Access is the Stuart Lake trailhead at the end of FR 7601, off Icicle Creek Road out of Leavenworth; the last few miles are rough dirt, washboarded by late summer, and the …

camps_on_file.name: Bridge Creek and Eightmile campgrounds, Icicle Creek Road
camps_on_file.notes: Given how unlikely a Colchuck or Core permit is on any given weekend, most parties on Backbone Ridge, Serpentine Arete or Colchuck Balanced Rock end up sleeping down on Icicle Creek Road and starting for the trailhead in the small hours. Both campgrounds sit on the drive in, before the FR 7601 turnoff, so the extra dri…

camps_on_file.name: Talus and boulder bivies below Dragontail's north side
camps_on_file.notes: Parties wanting to shorten the approach to Backbone Ridge or Serpentine Arete sometimes move above the lake into the boulders and moraine beneath the north face rather than staying at the shoreline camps. It buys perhaps half an hour and a clearer look at the route, at the cost of a colder, windier and rockier night. W…

days.title: Day 1
days.note: Drive to Ingalls Creek Trailhead and backpack in via the Ingalls Creek Trail and the Crystal Creek/Nightmare Gorge boot path to a camp in Crystal Creek Basin or at Crystal Lake.

days.title: Day 2
days.note: Climb the Southwest Rib (roughly 19 pitches) to the summit, then descend via the Westernmost Chessman to the Enchantment Plateau or back to Crystal Lake; return to camp.

days.title: Day 3
days.note: Hike out via Crystal Creek and Ingalls Creek Trail to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Crystal Creek basin below the Southwest Rib
camps_on_file.notes: Informal camping on the floor of Crystal Creek basin near the toe of the rib. Reach it by hiking up Crystal Creek from the Ingalls Creek trail, or by dropping south from Crystal Lake on the Enchantment plateau along its outlet stream.
